issues.legal_issue: A child of the husband from whom a female vendor inherited property is within the class entitled to pre-empt a sale of that property, even if the child was born to another wife.
material_facts: The female vendor inherited the property through her husband and later sold it.
The claimant was a daughter of that husband, but not of the female vendor.
The claimant sought possession by pre-emption of the property sold.
issues.conclusion: The claimant was entitled to exercise the right of pre-emption as a child of the husband from whom the vendor had inherited the property.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 15(2)(b) of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, the right is confined to the lineal descendants of the last male holder from whom the property came by inheritance. The reference to the female vendor’s son or daughter means the child of the husband through whom she inherited the property, including that husband’s child by another wife. This construction accords with the scheme described in Mote Singh v. Prem Parkash Kaur and the reasoning in Moti Ram v. Bakhwant Singh.

predicates.is_preemption_claim: A claimant seeks to exercise a right of pre-emption against a sale of property.
predicates.vendor_inherited_property_through_husban: The female vendor inherited the property through her husband before selling it.
predicates.claimant_is_child_of_that_husband: The claimant is a child of the husband through whom the vendor inherited the property, whether or not the claimant is also the vendor’s child.

issues.definition: When a pre-emption claimant is a child of the husband through whom the female vendor inherited the sold property, the claimant has a right of pre-emption.

issues.legal_issue: An amendment that clarifies the pre-existing meaning of the law governing pre-emption applies retrospectively.
material_facts: The claimant’s pre-emption suit was pending through appeals when the 1964 amendment was enacted.
The amendment inserted words identifying the relevant husband in the provision governing who could pre-empt a sale by a female vendor.
The Court concluded that the provision already referred to the children of the husband through whom the vendor inherited the property.
issues.conclusion: The 1964 amendment was clarificatory and had retrospective operation; in any event, the claimant was entitled under the provision even before the amendment.
issues.legal_principle: A curative or declaratory statute is more readily construed as having retrospective operation than legislation that prejudicially affects past rights and transactions. The Court relied on the interpretation of Section 15(2)(b) and the reasoning in Moti Ram v. Bakhwant Singh.

predicates.is_preemption_proceeding: A court is deciding a claim or appeal in a proceeding for pre-emption.
predicates.amendment_clarifies_preexisting_law: A later amendment clarifies the meaning the relevant law already had, rather than changing that meaning.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption proceeding, an amendment that clarifies the law’s pre-existing meaning applies retrospectively.

issues.legal_issue: A decree-conformity provision referring to an earlier amending enactment does not by its terms extend to amendments enacted later.
material_facts: A provision inserted in 1960 directed courts not to pass pre-emption decrees inconsistent with the provisions of that amending enactment.
A further amendment was enacted in 1964 while the pre-emption dispute was in the appellate process.
The Court read the reference to the “said Act” as referring to the 1960 enactment.
issues.conclusion: The 1960 decree-conformity provision did not, by its terms, cover amendments enacted after the 1960 enactment.
issues.legal_principle: Section 31 of the Punjab Pre-emption Act, inserted by the 1960 amendment, referred to the provisions of the “said Act.” The Court relied on Ram Sarup v. Munshi for the scope of that provision as to the 1960 amendments, but held that its wording did not extend to later amendments and that courts should not give it an unwarranted extended meaning.

predicates.is_preemption_proceeding: A court is deciding a claim or appeal in a proceeding for pre-emption.
predicates.decree_conformity_clause_refers_to_earli: A law directs courts to make pre-emption decrees conform to an enactment identified in that law.
predicates.later_amendment_enacted: A further amendment was enacted after the enactment identified by the decree-conformity clause.

issues.definition: In a pre-emption proceeding, a decree-conformity clause referring to an earlier enactment does not automatically cover a later amendment.
